{{Short description|German mathematician and artist (1940–2026)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2026}}
'''Gisela Engeln-Müllges''' (1940 – 31 January 2026) was a German mathematician and artist. She was a professor of numerical mathematics at the [[FH Aachen|Aachen University of Applied Sciences]], where she also was a vice rector for research, development, and technology.{{r|az}}

==Education and academic career==
Engeln-Müllges was born in [[Leipzig]] in 1940. After [[World War II]], Leipzig became part of East Germany (the [[German Democratic Republic]]), and Engeln-Müllges escaped to the west in 1961. She studied mathematics at [[RWTH Aachen University]] beginning in 1961,{{r|lab}} and completed a doctorate ([[Dr. rer. nat.]]) in 1971, with a dissertation ''Fluchtebenennomogramme zur Darstellung von Funktionensystemen: Ihre Theorie und praktische Verwendbarkeit'' concerning [[numerical analysis]].{{r|mg}}

She was a professor at the Aachen University of Applied Sciences from 1982, and was vice rector there from 1992 to 2005.{{r|lab|idw75}} With Frank Uhlig, she was the author of the books ''Numerik-Algorithmen mit C'' and ''Numerik-Algorithmen mit Fortran'' (7th ed., 1993, translated into English as ''Numerical Algorithms with Fortran'' and ''Numerical Algorithms with C'', Springer, 1996).{{r|temden|kk|pryce}}

==Art==
Engeln-Müllges's artworks are abstract, and include both paintings and cast-metal sculptures, based on her many years of work with artist {{ill|Benno Werth|de}}.{{r|az}} In 2019, she was one of the selected artists for the London Art Biennale.{{r|lab}}

==Death==
Engeln-Müllges died on 31 January 2026, at the age of 85.<ref>[https://www.fh-muenster.de/de/ueber-uns/newsroom/news/die-fh-muenster-trauert-um-ihre-ehemalige-langjaehrige-hochschulratsvorsitzende "Die FH Münster trauert um ihre ehemalige langjährige Hochschulratsvorsitzende"]. ''fh-muenster.de'', 3 February 2026 (in German). Retrieved 4 February 2026.</ref>

==Recognition==
Engeln-Müllges was awarded the Federal Cross of Merit in 1992.{{r|lab|idw75}} In 2005, she was given an honorary doctorate by [[Nizhny Novgorod State Technical University]].{{r|idw75}}
